questions.prompt: Locate the centroid of the plane area shown: a vertical $1\text{-in.}$-wide, $8\text{-in.}$-tall bar along the $y$ axis with a $1\text{-in.}$-thick horizontal arm reaching $4\,\text{in.}$ from the $y$ axis, its lower edge $2\,\text{in.}$ above the $x$ axis. Give $\bar{X}$ (in in.).
Locate the centroid of the plane area shown. Give $\bar{Y}$ (in mm).

Locate the centroid of the plane area shown: a $14\text{-in.}$-wide, $20\text{-in.}$-tall rectangle with a circular hole of radius $4\,\text{in.}$ centered $6\,\text{in.}$ from the $y$ axis and $12\,\text{in.}$ above the $x$ axis. Give $\bar{X}$ (in in.).
Locate the centroid of the semicircular ring shown ($r_1 = 8\,\text{in.}$, $r_2 = 12\,\text{in.}$). Give $\bar{Y}$ (in in.).
questions.solution:
By symmetry $\bar{X} = 0$. Treat the ring as a semicircle of radius $12$ minus a semicircle of radius $8$, each with $\bar{y} = 4r/3\pi$.

Outer: $A = \tfrac{\pi}{2}(144) = 226.2\,\text{in}^2$, $\bar{y} = 16/\pi = 5.093$, $\bar{y}A = 1152$. Inner: $A = -\tfrac{\pi}{2}(64) = -100.5$, $\bar{y} = 32/3\pi = 3.395$, $\bar{y}A = -341.3$.

$\bar{Y} = (1152 - 341.3)/(226.2 - 100.5) = 810.7/125.7 = 6.45\,\text{in.}$

questions.prompt: Locate the centroid of the area between the parabola $x = ky^2$ and the straight line shown ($a = 8\,\text{in.}$, $b = 4\,\text{in.}$; both curves pass through the origin and the point $(8, 4)$). Give $\bar{X}$ (in in.).
questions.solution:
Area = (region under the parabola $y = \sqrt{2x}$ down to the $x$ axis) $-$ (triangle under the line).

Parabolic region (semiparabolic area with its axis along $x$, so the table values $3h/5$ and $3a/8$ apply with the roles of $x$ and $y$ interchanged): $A_1 = \tfrac{2}{3}(8)(4) = 21.33\,\text{in}^2$, $\bar{x}_1 = \tfrac{3}{5}(8) = 4.8$, $\bar{y}_1 = \tfrac{3}{8}(4) = 1.5\,\text{in.}$

Triangle: $A_2 = -\tfrac{1}{2}(8)(4) = -16\,\text{in}^2$, $\bar{x}_2 = 16/3$, $\bar{y}_2 = 4/3\,\text{in.}$

$\Sigma A = 5.333\,\text{in}^2$; $\Sigma\bar{x}A = 102.4 - 85.33 = 17.07$; $\Sigma\bar{y}A = 32 - 21.33 = 10.67$.

$\bar{X} = 17.07/5.333 = 3.20\,\text{in.}$, $\bar{Y} = 10.67/5.333 = 2.00\,\text{in.}$

questions.prompt: Determine by direct integration the centroid of the area between the line $y = mx$ and the parabola $y = kx^2$ shown (they meet at $x = a$, $y = h$).
questions.solution:
$m = h/a$, $k = h/a^2$. Vertical strip: $dA = (y_1 - y_2)\,dx = h\left(\tfrac{x}{a} - \tfrac{x^2}{a^2}\right)dx$, $\bar{x}_{el} = x$, $\bar{y}_{el} = \tfrac{1}{2}(y_1 + y_2)$.

$A = h\left(\tfrac{a}{2} - \tfrac{a}{3}\right) = \tfrac{ah}{6}$. $\;Q_y = h\int_0^a\left(\tfrac{x^2}{a} - \tfrac{x^3}{a^2}\right)dx = h a^2\left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac14\right) = \tfrac{a^2h}{12}$, so $\bar{x} = a/2$.

$Q_x = \int\tfrac12(y_1^2 - y_2^2)\,dx = \tfrac{h^2}{2}\int_0^a\left(\tfrac{x^2}{a^2} - \tfrac{x^4}{a^4}\right)dx = \tfrac{h^2a}{2}\left(\tfrac13 - \tfrac15\right) = \tfrac{ah^2}{15}$, so $\bar{y} = \tfrac{ah^2/15}{ah/6} = \tfrac{2h}{5}$.

questions.prompt: Determine by direct integration the centroid of the shaded area shown, bounded by the quarter ellipse $x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1$ and the lines $y = b$ and $x = a$. Which expression gives $\bar{x}$?
questions.solution:
Area $= ab - \tfrac{\pi ab}{4} = ab\,\tfrac{4 - \pi}{4}$. The first moment about the $y$ axis equals that of the rectangle minus that of the quarter ellipse (centroid $4a/3\pi$): $Q_y = ab\tfrac{a}{2} - \tfrac{\pi ab}{4}\tfrac{4a}{3\pi} = \tfrac{a^2b}{2} - \tfrac{a^2b}{3} = \tfrac{a^2b}{6}$ (the same result follows by integrating vertical strips $dA = (b - y)\,dx$).

$\bar{x} = \dfrac{a^2b/6}{ab(4 - \pi)/4} = \dfrac{2a}{3(4 - \pi)}$, and by the same argument $\bar{y} = \dfrac{2b}{3(4 - \pi)}$.

questions.prompt: A $\tfrac{3}{4}\text{-in.}$-diameter hole is drilled in a piece of $1\text{-in.}$-thick steel; the hole is then countersunk ($90^\circ$ included angle, top diameter $1\tfrac{1}{4}\,\text{in.}$) as shown. Determine the volume of steel removed during the countersinking process (in $\text{in}^3$).
questions.solution:
The countersink removes the material generated by revolving a right triangle about the hole's axis. Its legs: radial $\tfrac12(1.25 - 0.75) = 0.25\,\text{in.}$ and (for a $90^\circ$ countersink, $45^\circ$ sides) depth $0.25\,\text{in.}$; area $A = \tfrac12(0.25)(0.25) = 0.03125\,\text{in}^2$.

Its centroid lies at $\bar{r} = 0.375 + \tfrac13(0.25) = 0.4583\,\text{in.}$ from the axis. By Theorem II of Pappus-Guldinus:

$$V = 2\pi\bar{r}A = 2\pi(0.4583)(0.03125) = 0.0900\,\text{in}^3.$$

questions.prompt: For the beam and loading shown (load varying parabolically from $2000\,\text{N/m}$ at $A$ to $900\,\text{N/m}$ at $B$, the parabola having its vertex at $B$; span $6\,\text{m}$), determine the distance from $A$ to the line of action of the resultant of the distributed load (in m).
questions.solution:
Split the load into a rectangle of height $900\,\text{N/m}$ and a parabolic spandrel of height $1100\,\text{N/m}$ at $A$ with vertex at $B$.

Rectangle: $R_1 = (900)(6) = 5400\,\text{N}$ at $3\,\text{m}$. Spandrel): $R_2 = \tfrac13(6)(1100) = 2200\,\text{N}$, centroid $\tfrac34(6) = 4.5\,\text{m}$ from the vertex $B$, i.e. $1.5\,\text{m}$ from $A$.

$R = 7600\,\text{N} = 7.60\,\text{kN}\downarrow$; $\;\bar{x} = \dfrac{5400(3) + 2200(1.5)}{7600} = \dfrac{19\,500}{7600} = 2.57\,\text{m}$.

Reactions: $B = 7600(2.566)/6 = 3.25\,\text{kN}\uparrow$, $A = 7.60 - 3.25 = 4.35\,\text{kN}\uparrow$.

questions.prompt: Determine the reaction at support $B$ (in N) for the beam and loading shown: over the middle $1.5\text{-m}$ segment (starting $0.4\,\text{m}$ right of $A$, ending $0.6\,\text{m}$ left of $B$) the load varies linearly from $400\,\text{N/m}$ upward to $900\,\text{N/m}$ downward.
questions.solution:
Represent the linear load as two triangles over the $1.5\text{-m}$ segment: an upward triangle with $400\,\text{N/m}$ at its left end, $R_1 = \tfrac12(1.5)(400) = 300\,\text{N}\uparrow$ at $0.4 + 0.5 = 0.9\,\text{m}$ from $A$; and a downward triangle with $900\,\text{N/m}$ at its right end, $R_2 = \tfrac12(1.5)(900) = 675\,\text{N}\downarrow$ at $0.4 + 1.0 = 1.4\,\text{m}$ from $A$. Span $AB = 2.5\,\text{m}$.

$+\circlearrowleft\sum M_A = 0$: $B(2.5) - 675(1.4) + 300(0.9) = 0 \Rightarrow B = 675/2.5 = 270\,\text{N}\uparrow$.

$+\uparrow\sum F_y = 0$: $A + 270 + 300 - 675 = 0 \Rightarrow A = 105.0\,\text{N}\uparrow$.

questions.prompt: Determine by direct integration the moment of inertia, with respect to the $y$ axis, of the shaded area under the curve $y = kx^{1/3}$ from $x = 0$ to $x = a$ (height $b$ at $x = a$).
questions.solution:
$b = ka^{1/3} \Rightarrow y = b(x/a)^{1/3}$. Vertical strip: every point is at distance $x$ from the $y$ axis, so $dI_y = x^2 y\,dx$.

$I_y = \int_0^a x^2\,\dfrac{b}{a^{1/3}}x^{1/3}\,dx = \dfrac{b}{a^{1/3}}\left[\dfrac{3}{10}x^{10/3}\right]_0^a = \dfrac{3a^3b}{10}$.

(Option C, $ab^3/6$, is $I_x$ of the same area — Prob. 9.6.)

questions.prompt: Determine the moment of inertia of the shaded area between $y_1 = k_1x^2$ and $y_2 = k_2x^{1/2}$ (which meet at $x = a$, $y = b$) with respect to the $x$ axis.
questions.solution:
$y_1 = b(x/a)^2$, $y_2 = b(x/a)^{1/2}$. A vertical strip is a thin rectangle from $y_1$ to $y_2$: $dI_x = \tfrac13(y_2^3 - y_1^3)\,dx$.

$I_x = \dfrac{b^3}{3}\int_0^a\left[\left(\tfrac{x}{a}\right)^{3/2} - \left(\tfrac{x}{a}\right)^6\right]dx = \dfrac{ab^3}{3}\left(\dfrac25 - \dfrac17\right) = \dfrac{3ab^3}{35}$.

With $A = \int (y_2 - y_1)\,dx = ab\left(\tfrac23 - \tfrac13\right) = \tfrac{ab}{3}$: $k_x = \sqrt{9/35}\,b$.

questions.prompt: Determine the polar radius of gyration of the trapezoidal area shown with respect to point $P$ (top width $2a$, bottom width $a$, height $a$, with $P$ at the midpoint of the bottom edge). Give $k_P$ as a multiple of $a$ (enter the coefficient).
questions.solution:
Take $x$ along the bottom edge and $y$ up, origin $P$. At height $y$ the width is $a + y$.

$I_x = \int_0^a y^2(a + y)\,dy = \tfrac{a^4}{3} + \tfrac{a^4}{4} = \tfrac{7a^4}{12}$.

$I_y$: each horizontal strip (half-width $(a+y)/2$, symmetric about the $y$ axis) contributes $\tfrac{1}{12}(a+y)^3\,dy$, so $I_y = \tfrac{1}{12}\int_0^a (a+y)^3\,dy = \tfrac{1}{48}(16a^4 - a^4) = \tfrac{15a^4}{48}$.

$J_P = I_x + I_y = \tfrac{28a^4}{48} + \tfrac{15a^4}{48} = \tfrac{43a^4}{48}$. With $A = \tfrac12(2a + a)a = \tfrac32a^2$: $k_P^2 = \tfrac{43a^4/48}{3a^2/2} = \tfrac{43}{72}a^2 \Rightarrow k_P = 0.773a$.

questions.prompt: Determine the moment of inertia of the shaded area with respect to the $x$ axis (top flange $24 \times 6\,\text{mm}$, bottom flange $48 \times 6\,\text{mm}$, web $8\,\text{mm}$ thick and $48\,\text{mm}$ tall, $x$ axis at mid-height of the web). Give $I_x$ in units of $10^3\,\text{mm}^4$.

Determine the moment of inertia $\bar{I}_y$ of the area shown with respect to the centroidal axis perpendicular to side $AB$ (a $108 \times 60\,\text{mm}$ rectangle with a triangular hole: vertical base $36\,\text{mm}$ located $22\,\text{mm}$ from the left side, apex $72\,\text{mm}$ to the right). Give $\bar{I}_y$ in units of $10^6\,\text{mm}^4$.

Determine the moment of inertia $\bar{I}_x$ of the area shown with respect to the centroidal axis parallel to side $AB$ (a $5.0 \times 8.0\,\text{in.}$ rectangle with a $2.0 \times 5.0\,\text{in.}$ rectangular hole located $0.9\,\text{in.}$ from the left side and $1.2\,\text{in.}$ below $AB$). Give $\bar{I}_x$ in $\text{in}^4$.
